key_idea: The parity of the sum is the parity of the number of odd terms: odd N gives either, N = 2 mod 4 always has an odd count of odds, N = 0 mod 4 always an even count.
sketch: N consecutive integers contain N/2 odd numbers when N is even, regardless of the start, so the sum is odd iff N/2 is odd. When N is odd the number of odd terms depends on the parity of the start, and both starts are available in 1..100 for N <= 10, so the answer is Either. So: N odd -> Either, N mod 4 == 2 -> Odd, N mod 4 == 0 -> Even. O(1).
